mod_sources.key: F62 native national-idea names/descriptions, separately keyed sets; locator envelope

english_verification.review_scope: Representative current-Mod checks for the 1444 royal household, the 1446 mission condition, the optional U01 mission swap, Ahati disaster, and exact current English spellings Castan Beastbane, Crodamic dynasty, and Elikhetist; read three relevant fixed-revision English Wiki chunks for Nirakhet, Aakhet, and Ahati background. F64 retention and the 29-mission count follow the supplied evidence; no exhaustive task-tree audit was performed. The primary compared native idea names/descriptions with current English localisation keys (formatting codes stripped); original sources and optional sets are kept separate. Wide source bounds are locator envelopes, not exhaustive line-by-line audits. No formal validators, tests, builds or browser checks were run.
unresolved: No dedicated Duwarkani country page was located in the supplied evidence; the checked Wiki pages provide related historical and religious context only.
The 1446 mission gate is not the date of the royal marriage or territorial annexation; those exact dates remain unestablished.
The Wiki's later setting outcomes do not guarantee a player-campaign ending.
Ahati disaster duration and AI diplomacy have not been measured in-game.

rationale.campaign_length: The 29 direct missions make for a medium-length tree with dense storytelling but a relatively abrupt ending.
rationale.colonization: The route has almost no colonisation loop.
rationale.complexity: Racial tolerance, cultural acceptance, religion, estate privileges, Guardianship mandate, and the disaster must be managed in parallel.
rationale.dark_story: The Shadow Swamp, assassination, a history of genocide, and the dead are grim, but the country’s own route centres on protection and redemption.
rationale.difficulty: The opening survival challenge and Ahati disaster are dangerous, though military and economic strength improve considerably after stabilising.
rationale.diplomacy: Relations with Samsumbat, balancing stronger neighbours, and the Guardianship system require alliance and diplomatic planning.
rationale.early_pressure: A small country is surrounded by stronger neighbours and powerful mages; the opening war and alliance windows leave little room for error.
rationale.magic_artifice_intensity: Mage towers, Delta Gnomish orbs, anti-ballistic amulets, powerful mage neighbours, and the Shadowrealm all play major roles.
rationale.narrative_density: The royal assassination, harpy succession, Aakhet revelation, interspecies conflict, and Beastbane’s redemption form a complete story.
rationale.tall_play: The gold mine, magic-resource sites, forts, holy sites, and wonders matter, but cannot replace regional expansion.
rationale.trade_economy: Gnoll caravans, Sadra trade, and resource-province development help, but do not form a separate core mechanic.
rationale.warfare: Reclaiming the Sadra, fighting mages and stronger neighbours, suppressing the Ahati revolt, and entering the Shadow Swamp all require sustained warfare.

identity.appearance: A human–harpy co-ruled kingdom in 1444; it may form F64 Prakheta while retaining this mission tree.

successors.relationship: Optional continuous formable: the decision retains Duwarkani’s mission tree but changes its national ideas.

national_ideas.scope_note: National traditions, seven national ideas and ambition only; optional idea groups and racial/government bonuses are excluded. Conditional alternatives are separate, not stacked. Accepting new ideas on formation depends on the actual event/decision and player choice.

description.text: The Upholders of Ma'at were a holy order of harpy warriors whose mission was to guard the khetist faithful who ventured away from the Sorrow. Most of the order died at the hands of Grizaka's army during the siege of Golkora, but a small chapter survived in Duwarkani and refounded themselves as the Feathers of Ma'at to commemorate the martyred bodies of their sisters.

description.text: Duwarkani is known for its hardy herdsmen and their distinctive red-furred camels. This local breed is well suited to the rocky and treacherous terrain of the mountainsides and the sparse forage found there. Duwarkani men are often away from home for months, driving the camels to foraging spots while hunting game from atop their mounts. The skill with which these men handle their animals and the capabilities of the breed make them fierce opponents in the twisting valleys and ravines, appearing at will from behind hills and crags to pour arrow-fire into the enemy.

description.text: Duwarkani is the southern outpost of the khetist faith. Responsible for guarding Kheterata from lizardfolk incursions and ensuring the safety of pilgrims traveling through Khetapera. Now that Grizaka's war has sundered the empire, this mission remains. Protect the faithful. Guard Kheterata. Guide the pilgrims.

description.text: The wives and daughters of the Duwarkani’s villages maintain large gardens built into the mountainsides. They compete with each other to display the wealth of their village through gaudy arrangements of flowers and carved heads that trumpet a village's name and wealth to distant travelers or rivals the valley over. There is no sight more beloved in Duwarkani than to glimpse one’s garden after a long journey.

description.text:
The greatest Steward in all of Kheterata’s long history started life as a simple Irsmahapan soldier. Serving at a time when Kheterata was forced to kowtow to the upstart slaves in Castanor, Menkaunswt’s many successes would see him rise through the ranks at an unprecedented speed, until he could depose the traitorous Steward and reclaim Kheterata’s pride. His 65 year-long reign would see the Castanorians pushed back, Akasik and much of Bulwar subjugated, a bloom in relations with the Hierarchy, the birth of the Ahati and Kheteratan gem magic, and the integration of the Delta Gnomes and Nzeri Harpies into Kheteratan society.

While the rule of Menkaunswt’s dynasty ended with the Damerian invasion, his name still carried enough power that the Crodamic rulers saw fit to banish what remained of the family to most remote part of Kheterata they could think of: the distant fortress city at the very edge of the Shadow Swamp, known as Duwarkani. Here his descendants still rule, heirs to a lineage surpassed only by the khet themselves!

description.text: Humans and harpies have long lived side by side in Duwarkani, with the human governors and harpy matriarchs each ruling their respective peoples in the name of the Stewards. But with the authority of Kheterata gone, and no Stewards to command governor and matriarch, both sides agreed that a closer union was needed to ensure a united leadership of Duwarkani. With the marriage of Lord Kenmu and Lady Safana, the dynasty of Menkausnwt and the Duwaran dynasty which has ruled the Nzeri since the year 600 have now united into one. Thus was born an heir worthy to rule all of Duwarkani, and perhaps even all of Kheterata...

description.text: Lightly equipped harpy targeters combined with camel mounted heavy guns allow the armies of Duwarkani to turn the mountains into deathtraps. The harpies mark their targets with thrown burning alchemical flares or pots of colored dust, prompting the fire of the battery on priority targets.

description.text: Once, the Crodamic dynasty were the grandest servants of the Khet, showing the light of the Khet for the very first time to the people of Khetapera and Horashesh. But even the most illustrious dynasties can fall to decadence, and the Crodamics were sadly no different. Stewards wasted men in petty wars with Bulwari and Cannorians while the forces of evil and corruption were waiting right outside their borders, secluded High Priests proclaimed stiff doctrines with no regard for the common worshipper, and the most holy Khetarch Baqtkhet I’s decision to promise the crown to Jaher led to centuries of heathens claiming ownership over Kheterata. Our new kingdom is a chance to start fresh again, with a government that understands the true needs of the land and its people. May it not repeat the mistakes of the past.

description.text: The Stewards of the Sorrow have traditionally ruled from the great city of Kheterat, reportedly built by Elikhet himself near the ruins of a genie city. Yet there can be no holier city than Niramit, located at the very Source of the Mother’s Sorrow, the birthplace of the great river that gives life to Kheterata and even to the Khet themselves. Beyond the city’s religious significance, its simultaneous location on the shores of both the Mother’s Sorrow and Lake Nirakhet does wonders for our administration’s ability to send people to and from every corner of our kingdom on a good timeframe.

description.text: As the demonic gnolls of Gnollakaz invaded Irsmahap and most of the southern nobility was slaughtered in battle, the cities of Khetapera were both cut off from the central authority of Kheterata and bereft of the region’s traditional ruling class. Left to fend for themselves, the different cities started waging war on each over their different visions for what rule of the region should look like. These wars carried unique difficulties due to the many mountain fortifications across the region. Learning how to siege these mountain forts and maneuvering through the narrow mountain passes that they guard have given our generals unmatched skill in besting the difficult conditions of this region.

description.text: The forces of evil are ever at our doorstep. In the savannah, the gnolls prepare their sacrificial pyres for their infernal masters. In the swamp, the hags plot their schemes with troll slave and human pawn alike. The Crodamics failed to truly understand the threat of the darkness at their borders, and it ultimately cost them everything. We must never repeat their grave mistake. Our soldiers must always be ready to keep the forces of chaos at bay, and our rulers must never forget what is at stake should they lapse in their focus.

description.text: Elikhet’s Decree on Magic is possibly the most widely interpreted and debated of all his decrees. While everyone after the end of the Damerian Occupation and Elikhet’s Return would agree that the Decree stresses the importance of the mages to use their divine gift for the benefit of the Khet and Kheterata instead of corrupting it for their own selfish desires, the specifics on how to enforce it varies wildly. The Decree has been used as justification for stripping mages of their freedom and turning them into bound labor, investing vast powers and privileges to a magical oversight committee staffed by the most trustworthy mages, and everything in between. This controversy would come to a head during the splintering of Khetapera, when it became a dividing line between the newly independent cities, which in turn would serve as justification for war between them. To avoid similar conflicts in the future, we need to use our authority as Stewards of Kheterata to hand down the definitive interpretation of the Decree, so that there can be no future doubt on the proper use of the divine gift.

description.text: In the south of Kheterata, the Ahati serve a somewhat different role than they do in the north. As the merchants of the south needed protection from gnollish raids, and the Ahati wished for further autonomy from Kheterat, the two would eventually join together, forming trade guilds ruled by the Ahati code of honor. We weren’t aware of what a blessing this was until the splintering of Kheterata, when much of the treacherous northern merchant class threw their lot in with the heathen pretenders of Elizna. Such blasphemous treachery is unacceptable in Prakheta. It is clear that we need to expand the system of Ahati merchant guilds to all of The Sorrow, so that the northern merchants may finally learn some honor and discipline.

description.text: Perhaps the most impressive feat of the Crodamics before their downfall was just how far they managed to spread the light of the Khet. Their domain from sea to sea, possessing fleets in both Koroshesh in the north and Zuvavim in the south. But the great distance from Kheterat to Horashesh, further separated by the mountains of Khetapera, made it impossible for the Stewards to directly manage the region. Instead, they relied on a system of appointed governors ruling the local satrapies alongside local rulers. This proved disastrous for the region once Grizaka cut off the path from Horashesh to Kheterat. With no royal aid to keep the governors in line and help them enforce order, all of Horashesh quickly descended into chaos, with both governors turning on each other and the local kings scrambling to usurp power from the royal governors. Luckily, with our capital much further south, we can govern the region in a more direct and unified manner. The Horasheshi can rest easy knowing that unlike the previous Kheterata, we will never lose control over their land.

player_overview.avoid_if: Avoid if you dislike estate privileges, severe disasters, cultural and religious requirements, or want a mission tree extending to global conquest.
player_overview.how_it_plays: Survive early through terrain, alliances, and limited wars; advance north in the middle game to claim Guardianship and handle the Ahati crisis; later integrate peoples through conversion and acceptance, cleanse the Shadow Swamp, and complete Beastbane’s story.
player_overview.overview: You are a small human–harpy co-ruled state on the edge of the Shadow Swamp, descended from the exiled royal house of ancient Kheterata. First survive between stronger neighbours and mages; then place a harpy heir on the throne, reclaim the Sadra, and rebuild the Ahati. In the middle and late game, bring gnolls, lizardfolk, gnomes, and trolls into the state as equals, withstand an Ahati revolt, cleanse the Shadow Swamp, and make the legendary monster-slayer Castan Beastbane confront his legacy of genocide.
player_overview.recommended_for: Players who enjoy a difficult small-country start, strong storytelling, harpy military, multi-ethnic institutions, religious idealism, and Shadowrealm exploration.
signature_features: Human administration and harpy warfare coexist, including a rare harpy route retaining cavalry while developing flying armies.
Integrating each people unlocks corresponding estate privileges and national abilities, ultimately bringing five peoples into one political community.
An expedition into the Shadowrealm investigates the World Tree, hags, Shadow Trolls, and Castan Beastbane, reversing the traditional hero narrative through forgiveness.
player_overview.tagline: Give a human dynasty harpy wings and build a Sadra realm where paladins, the Ahati, and Nirakhet’s tears abolish the boundary between people and monsters.

reasons: Multi-ethnic equality is built into mission requirements, estate privileges, and army composition—not just background lore.
Human cavalry and harpy armies create an unusual military playstyle.
Aakhet, the Ahati, and Beastbane connect Kheteratan and Castanorian history in a densely written narrative.
The Shadow Swamp expedition and final act of forgiveness offer an uncommon heroic route.
warnings: You begin small and surrounded by stronger neighbours; securing a war window, allies, or mercenaries is often necessary.
The Ahati disaster can severely damage the economy, army, and ability to take diplomatic action.
Numerous estate privileges and conversion and cultural-acceptance requirements can slow mission progress.
The story is excellent but the tree is only medium in length and ends relatively abruptly.

positive_indicators: The army refuses to suppress civilians.
values.rationale: The route institutionalises the inclusion of humans, harpies, gnolls, lizardfolk, gnomes, and trolls, and emphasises protecting civilians, repentance, and forgiveness. It is among the strongest examples of universal personhood in the current sample.
red_flags: Regional conquest and religious integration still occur.
